script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: identity

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. FISHER KITCHEN - MORNING

SARA FISHER, 30s, an architect, and JACK FISHER, 60s, a retired teacher, sit around their kitchen table as the sun streams in through the window.

SARA
(cheerfully)
Good morning, Dad.

JACK
(smiling)
Good morning, dear. What do we have planned for today?

Sara pulls out a sketchbook from her bag, revealing a detailed architectural design.

SARA
I've got a presentation for a new community project today. It's a chance to make a real difference in people's lives.

JACK
(proudly)
I've always known you'd make a great impact on the world, Sara.

INT. FISHER LIVING ROOM - AFTERNOON

Sara and Jack are watching an old home video. The scene shows a young Sara, holding her father's hand as they walk along a beach.

SARA
(wistfully)
Do you ever think about where my mother would be if she were still alive?

JACK
(sighs)
Every day, Sara. But we can't change the past. All we can do is make the most of the present and cherish the memories.

INT. SCHOOL - DAY

Sara is giving a presentation to a group of students about her community project. She discusses the importance of sustainable living and community engagement.

INT. FISHER LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Sara sits on the couch with a worried expression, looking at an old photo album. She flips through the pages, stopping at a picture of her and Jack on the beach.

SARA
(to herself)
What if Dad's right? What if all we can do is make the most of the present? But what about my past? Who am I if not the sum of my memories?

INT. FISHER KITCHEN - MORNING

Sara makes breakfast for Jack and herself. They sit and eat together, sharing stories about their day.

SARA
(smiling)
You know, Dad, I think you're right. We can't change the past, but we can make sure our present is filled with love, laughter, and meaningful experiences.

JACK
(tearing up)
I'm so proud of you, Sara.

INT. FISHER LIVING ROOM - EVENING

Sara and Jack are once again watching their old home video. This time, they watch as a young Sara helps Jack build a sandcastle on the beach.

SARA
(smiling)
Do you remember this, Dad?

JACK
(laughing)
Of course. I'll never forget the day my little girl taught me how to build a sandcastle.

INT. COMMUNITY CENTER - NIGHT

Sara presents her community project to a packed room of community members. She speaks passionately about her vision for a sustainable and engaged community.

INT. FISHER LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Sara and Jack sit together on the couch, holding hands and looking at each other.

JACK
Sara, you've made such a difference in this community. I'm so proud of you.

SARA
(tearing up)
I couldn't have done it without you, Dad.

They share a long, loving embrace.

FADE OUT.
